s463: Main diesel engine, steam/gas turbine or diesel-electric propulsion
s464: Before the watch: check the oil level, the sea/oil cooling water circuits and the fuel viscosity heating.
s465: Start-up: verify that the turning gear is disengaged and that the lube oil pressure and jacket water temperature are within operating limits.
s466: At sea: monitor the exhaust temperature trends and carry out the cylinder balance check regularly; log vibration/alarm records.
s467: Shutdown: reduce the load gradually and keep circulating the cooling circuits according to the normal stopping procedure.
s468: Auxiliary diesel and emergency generators, shaft generator
s469: Complete the oil, cooling water, fuel and air/fog tests before starting.
s470: Keep harmonic/reactive loads balanced by monitoring generator load sharing.
s471: Carry out the emergency generator auto-start and fuel level tests weekly.
s472: Record the AVR, governor and insulation resistance tests during planned maintenance.
s473: Main/emergency switchboard, UPS, transformers and battery banks
s474: Apply the busbar synchronisation and breaker opening/closing sequences according to the procedure.
s475: Monitor harmonic distortion and voltage balance during load transfer; check overheating busbars with a thermal camera.
s476: Carry out UPS battery tests periodically, ventilate the room and check the gas detectors.
s477: Run black-out scenarios in emergency drills and record the times taken.
s478: Fuel/lube oil separators, day tanks, transfer and supply pumps
s479: Set the pre-separator heater according to the grade of fuel; make sure the bowl speed is at its nominal value.
s480: Apply an automatic shut-off and a lookout against the risk of overflow when transferring between day tanks.
s481: Record fouling trends by monitoring the LO/FO filtration differential pressures.
s482: Carry out sludge and drain discharges in accordance with the MARPOL procedure and enter them in the Oil Record Book.
s483: Bilge, ballast, fire, cooling water and fresh/sea water pumps
s484: Check the suction/discharge valves and any venting needs before starting each pump.
s485: Follow the tank sequence on the ballast pumps according to the stability plan; test the fire pumps weekly.
s486: Clean the strainers/filters on the cooling water pumps regularly and log the pressure and temperature differences.
s487: Verify the bilge pumps together with the MARPOL requirements and the 15 ppm OWS interlocks.
s488: Central cooling circuit, HVAC, cold stores and reefer systems
s489: Monitor the central cooling plate heat exchangers by differential pressure and clean them when necessary.
s490: Check the HVAC filters and damper settings monthly; adjust the fresh air ratio according to the CO₂ sensors.
s491: Verify the reefer socket load tests and the alarm monitoring panel regularly.
s492: Inspect the condenser/evaporator surfaces for fouling and record the gas leak tests.
s493: Auxiliary boiler and EGB; heating, fuel viscosity and steam demand
s494: Verify the steam/air pressure and viscosity required for fuel atomisation before starting up.
s495: Test the low water level and high steam pressure alarms periodically; observe the feed water pumps.
s496: Plan and record soot-blowing on the EGB according to the exhaust temperature difference.
s497: Monitor the TDS/pH values with a daily blow-down; adjust the chemical dosage according to the test results.
s498: Fire detection/CO₂, ECR operation, alarm and monitoring systems
s499: Use the alarm panel inhibit/override modes only where the procedure requires it; log any changes made.
s500: Verify the CO₂/FM200 system isolation valves, pull pins and siren tests periodically.
s501: Practise the changeover from the ECR to local control mode together with the crew.
s502: Review the trend records (pressure, temperature, vibration) weekly and update the early warning limits.
s503: Windlass, mooring winch, crane, capstan and Ro-Ro ramps
s504: Check the limit switches, oil levels and safety pins before the operation; barrier off the working area.
s505: Verify the mooring winch brake tests and the SWL labels periodically, and grease the wire ropes.
s506: Share the communication procedure and hand signals with the team during crane and ramp operations.
s507: Complete the hydraulic system pressure/leak checks; point out the emergency stop and manual override positions.
s876: Read the chapters, which progress from the legal framework to the logic of the article, and from the shipboard equivalent to case resolution. Each chapter closes with a reference, a common mistake and an operational outcome.
s878: After the comprehensive lesson, revise the main concepts quickly with the existing summary sections.
s881: Follow each requirement through its legal basis, safety rationale, responsible roles, objective evidence and verification steps.
s883: Instead of a one-off inspection preparation, build a lasting system that runs from applicability through to change management.
s885: See not only the text of the answer but also the evidence that has to be shown and the red flags that can trigger a detailed inspection.
s894: In an inspection, show the ship-specific practice rather than a memorised sentence: which provision applies, who is responsible, how the operation is carried out, which record is created and how safety is preserved in the event of a failure?

s969: Fire fighting appliances (FFA) must be complete.
s970: Fire doors and divisions must be checked regularly.
s971: Fire plans must be posted in visible locations.
s972: Fire extinguishers must be serviced regularly.
s973: Liferafts and lifeboats must be serviced regularly.
s974: Lifejackets must be available for all crew.
s975: EPIRB and SART devices must be in working order.
s976: Emergency position indicating beacons (EPIRB) must be registered.
s977: Immersion suits and thermal protective aids must be carried in sufficient numbers.
s978: The DOC (Document of Compliance) must be valid for the company.
s979: The SMC (Safety Management Certificate) must be valid for the ship.
s981: Internal audits must be carried out annually.
s982: The SSP (Ship Security Plan) must be approved and implemented.
s983: An SSO (Ship Security Officer) must be appointed.
s984: Security drills must be held regularly.
